ops.body:
**Symptom.** Claude Code on yasyf-home (ccp v0.53.0, app cask 0.52.0, macOS 26.4.1) failed to read `~/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-13/settings.json` with EDEADLK. All six hostsync-materialized FP accounts (acct-11..16, created Jul 13 22:11–22:12 during the origin-owned-sync migration) had `SF_DATALESS` content; enumeration worked, materialization failed instantly. acct-11 appeared healthy only because a 02:38 session had fully hydrated it — zero dataless files left.

**Timeline.**
- Jul 13 22:08:32 — daemon (fresh v0.53.0) logs `file provider bridge: socket …/Group Containers/SXKCTF23Q2.ccp/b.sock did not come up within 3s`.
- Jul 13 22:12:35–36 — TCC `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData` rows written for `/Users/yasyf/.cc-pool/bin/cc-pool` + Cellar/0.53.0 (auth_value 5, auth_reason 2); one second later `bridge v0.53.0 started; socket=…/b.sock … is up`. Bridge serves overnight; acct-11 hydrates at 02:38.
- Jul 14 04:21:02 — `file provider companion app is down; launching /Applications/CCPoolStatus.app in the background`. From the next session start (04:44, select → acct-13) every materialization fails EDEADLK **even though the daemon still held b.sock**.
- 04:59 `ccp fp repair --account 13` (re-register): no effect on reads — expected, since repair rides the CONTROL plane (`domains.sock`, app-bound, ungated) while content rides the DATA plane (`b.sock`).
- 05:01+ daemon restarts (brew services): bind of b.sock fails reproducibly with the "awaiting app-group-container consent" message; `ccp fp onboard` over SSH spins at "waiting for the CCPoolStatus app to come up" even while the app serves `domains.sock`.

**Remediation applied (one-off, machine-level).** `ccp fp repair --retreat --account N` for N=13,12,14,15,16 — the designed symlink-floor escape hatch. Safe here: those five accounts were 100% dataless (nothing local to lose) and session-free apart from acct-13's already-wedged claude. All six accounts read OK after; acct-11 left on FP (live sessions, fully hydrated). First new session (05:12:27, cc-steer → acct-14) ran normally.

**Mechanism (code recon, v0.53.0).**
- `b.sock` is bound by the DAEMON; the sandboxed appex is the client that dials it in fetchContents. `pool.FPBridgeSocketPath()` → `~/Library/Group Containers/SXKCTF23Q2.ccp/b.sock` (`internal/pool/paths.go:230-234`, `AppGroupID` at `:205`). The control socket `~/.cc-pool/domains.sock` is the mirror image: APP binds, daemon dials (`paths.go:223-228`) — hence control ops (doctor ✓, fp repair) succeeding while content is dead.
- Bind path: `startFPBridge` (`internal/daemon/fileprovider.go:49`) → `serveFPBridge` (`:97`): `os.MkdirAll` + `content.BridgeServer.Run` (fusekit `content/bridge.go`, `proc.SingleEntrant.Listen`) in a capped-backoff loop; `os.ErrPermission` = TCC-parked signature → retry silently; only non-permission errors latch `fpBridgeHardErr` (`fileprovider.go:97-123`).
- The 3s wait: `startFPBridge` dials its own socket via `content.NewBridgeClient(sock).Available()` every 20ms for `defaultFPBridgeWait = 3s` (`:38,:49-79`); on timeout without hard error it sets `fpConsentPending=true`, logs the consent line, and a 250ms watchdog (`:41`) polls until bind. `fpBridgeReady()` gates all FP probing on `!fpConsentPending && Available()` (`:350-360`).
- Ranked root cause: (1) PRIMARY — bind permission-parked: group-container consent is cdhash/GUI-session-sensitive; the launchd daemon never gets a visible prompt, so `serveFPBridge` parks forever. TCC AppData rows for the exact stable path EXIST (since Jul 13 22:12 PDT) yet the bind is still denied — the same binary bound successfully at 22:12:36 one second after those rows were written (almost certainly a foreground/GUI-context approval during `ccp fp onboard`/init), so rows-on-disk ≠ effective grant for the launchd context. (2) SECONDARY, post-bridge-restore only — possible per-domain fileproviderd replica poison from cold-bridge first fetches at 22:11; the heal ladder can't see it because `ProbeDomain` is a byte-count control op, not a materializing read (`internal/overlay/fpprobe.go`; fusekit `fileproviderd/appclient.go:121`). (3) REJECTED — app 0.52.0 vs CLI 0.53.0 skew: `MinWidgetVersion = "v0.44.0"` (`internal/pool/overlay.go:38`) passes, bridge wire frozen at `BridgeProtoVersion=1` (fusekit `content/bridge.go`). Hygiene, not cause.
- Unexplained residue: 04:21→05:01 the OLD daemon HELD b.sock yet materializations failed EDEADLK — a bound-but-dead bridge state the consent story doesn't cover (in-memory wedge coinciding with the companion-app death; daemon-side accept/serve state lost at restart, not diagnosable post-hoc).

**Code-fix evidence index (for the fix in flight).**
1. Bridge bind/wedge: `internal/daemon/fileprovider.go:34/:38/:41` consts, `:49` startFPBridge, `:97` serveFPBridge, `:350` fpBridgeReady, `:362` fpBridgeUp; `internal/daemon/registry.go:199-216` startupTable (`bridge.content`/`bridge.fp` before FP enumeration; `fp.app.ensure`); `internal/daemon/fpapp.go:77` shouldEnsureFPApp, `:123` ensureFPAppAsync.
2. fp onboard app-probe rung: `internal/cli/fileprovider.go:353` runFPOnboard → `:369` awaitFPCapability (`:484`, throwaway-domain probe via `:96` fpCapabilityProbe → fusekit `fileproviderd/appclient.go:105` Probe) → `:373` checkFPRungs (`:528`; `:546` reads fpDaemonProbe bridgeUp, `:555` pending/consent branch); `fpDaemonProbe` at `:79`.
3. Fix-shape note: a permission-parked bind is surfaced only as a log line + `fpConsentPending`; no lever exists to obtain the consent from launchd (prompt suppressed). Fix likely needs (a) a user-session path to trigger/approve the consent (foreground bind or onboard step), and/or (b) doctor/onboard detecting "bridge parked on consent" as a distinct rung with the foreground-approve→restart runbook; also (c) the bound-but-dead wedge needs a data-plane self-check (an Available()-style self-dial is not enough — it succeeded while serving was dead) and (d) `fp repair` could grow a bridge-health rung so re-register isn't offered when the bridge can't serve anyway.

**Residual state on yasyf-home.** acct-12..16 parked on symlink with pending user browser-logins; migrate back to FP (`ccp migrate --to fileprovider`) only after the bridge fix ships AND the consent is re-approved in a GUI session. acct-11 still FP-backed with the bridge down: reads fine (hydrated), but provider-upstream/new-content serving is queued until the bridge binds again. Daemon also loops `deferring stranded-bridge heal` on acct-01/02/07/10 (live sessions) — pre-existing, untouched. Selection still routes to credential-less accounts (needs-login clear bug) — parallel agent owns.
